text: Della finished her cry. <break time="0.8s" /> And powdered her cheeks. <break time="0.8s" /> She stood by the window. <break time="0.8s" /> And looked out sadly. <break time="0.8s" /> At a gray cat. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking along a gray fence. <break time="0.8s" /> In a gray backyard. <break time="0.8s" /> Tomorrow would be Christmas Day. <break time="0.8s" /> And she had only one dollar and eighty seven cents. <break time="0.8s" /> To buy Jim a present. <break time="0.8s" /> She had been saving every penny. <break time="0.8s" /> She could for months. <break time="0.8s" /> And this was the result. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly she turned from the window. <break time="0.8s" /> And stood before the mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> Her eyes were shining brilliantly. <break time="0.8s" /> But her face had lost its color. <break time="0.8s" /> Quickly she pulled down her hair. <break time="0.8s" /> And let it fall. <break time="0.8s" /> To its full length. <break time="0.8s" /> The James Dillingham Youngs. <break time="0.8s" /> Had two possessions. <break time="0.8s" /> In which they both took great pride. <break time="0.8s" /> One was Jims gold watch. <break time="0.8s" /> Which had belonged. <break time="0.8s" /> To his father and his grandfather. <break time="0.8s" /> The other. <break time="0.8s" /> Was Dellas hair. <break time="0.8s" /> It fell about her. <break time="0.8s" /> Rippling and shining. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a brown waterfall. <break time="0.8s" /> And reached below her knee.
